description: Design a simple 2-bit branch predictor that uses a 2-bit saturating counter. The predictor has two states: strongly taken, weakly taken, weakly not taken, and strongly not taken. The input signal is a branch instruction, which will either be taken (1) or not taken (0). The output will indicate the prediction (1 for taken, 0 for not taken) based on the current state of the predictor.
code:
module branch_predictor (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input branch_taken,
    output reg prediction
);
    reg [1:0] state;

    // State Encoding
    localparam ST_STRONGLY_TAKEN = 2'b11,
               ST_WEAKLY_TAKEN = 2'b10,
               ST_WEAKLY_NOT_TAKEN = 2'b01,
               ST_STRONGLY_NOT_TAKEN = 2'b00;

    // Update state based on branch outcome
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= ST_STRONGLY_NOT_TAKEN; // Reset state
            prediction <= 0; // Default prediction
        end else begin
            case (state)
                ST_STRONGLY_TAKEN: begin
                    if (branch_taken) begin
                        prediction <= 1; // Predict taken
                    end else begin
                        state <= ST_WEAKLY_TAKEN; // Move to weakly taken
                        prediction <= 1; // Predict taken
                    end
                end
                ST_WEAKLY_TAKEN: begin
                    if (branch_taken) begin
                        state <= ST_STRONGLY_TAKEN; // Move to strongly taken
                        prediction <= 1; // Predict taken
                    end else begin
                        state <= ST_WEAKLY_NOT_TAKEN; // Move to weakly not taken
                        prediction <= 1; // Predict taken
                    end
                end
                ST_WEAKLY_NOT_TAKEN: begin
                    if (branch_taken) begin
                        state <= ST_WEAKLY_TAKEN; // Move to weakly taken
                        prediction <= 0; // Predict not taken
                    end else begin
                        state <= ST_STRONGLY_NOT_TAKEN; // Move to strongly not taken
                        prediction <= 0; // Predict not taken
                    end
                end
                ST_STRONGLY_NOT_TAKEN: begin
                    if (branch_taken) begin
                        state <= ST_WEAKLY_NOT_TAKEN; // Move to weakly not taken
                        prediction <= 0; // Predict not taken
                    end else begin
                        prediction <= 0; // Predict not taken
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

Design a PCIe interface controller that manages the transmission of data packets. The controller should keep track of the current state of the transmission, which can be either IDLE, TRANSMITTING, or COMPLETE. The state transitions are as follows:
- From IDLE to TRANSMITTING on a signal `start`.

module pcie_controller (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire start,
    input wire done,
    input wire [15:0] data_in,
    output reg [15:0] data_out,
    output reg state // 0: IDLE, 1: TRANSMITTING, 2: COMPLETE
);
    parameter IDLE = 0, TRANSMITTING = 1, COMPLETE = 2;
    
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            data_out <= 16'b0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start) begin
                        state <= TRANSMITTING;
                        data_out <= data_in;
                    end
                end
                TRANSMITTING: begin
                    if (done) begin
                        state <= COMPLETE;
                    end
                end
                COMPLETE: begin
                    // Wait for the next start signal
                    state <= IDLE;
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a Verilog module that implements a Depth-First Search (DFS) algorithm on a fixed-size binary tree. The module should take an input signal to initiate the search and should have outputs to indicate the visited nodes and the search path taken. The binary tree is represented using a state machine, and the DFS should explore the left child before the right child. The module should have a clock input and a reset input to control the search operation.
code:
module DFS (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire start,
    output reg [3:0] visited,
    output reg [3:0] path
);
    reg [3:0] stack; // Stack to hold the nodes
    reg [1:0] state; // State variable

    parameter IDLE = 2'b00, VISIT = 2'b01, BACKTRACK = 2'b10;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            visited <= 0;
            path <= 0;
            stack <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start) begin
                        // Start DFS
                        stack <= 4'b0001; // Begin with root node
                        state <= VISIT;
                    end
                end
                VISIT: begin
                    if (stack != 0) begin
                        // Pop the top node from the stack
                        visited <= stack;
                        path <= path | stack; // Mark as visited
                        stack <= stack >> 1; // Move to the next node (left child)
                    end else begin
                        state <= BACKTRACK; // No more nodes to visit, backtrack
                    end
                end
                BACKTRACK: begin
                    // Backtrack by popping nodes until stack is empty
                    if (stack == 0) begin
                        state <= IDLE; // Finished DFS
                    end else begin
                        visited <= stack;
                        path <= path | stack;
                        stack <= stack >> 1; // Move to right child
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

    input wire reset,
    input wire [1:0] policy_select, // 0 = LRU, 1 = FIFO

);
    reg [3:0] lru_counter [0:15]; // For LRU
    reg [3:0] fifo_queue [0:15]; // For FIFO

        if (reset) begin
            for (i = 0; i < 16; i = i + 1) begin
                lru_counter[i] = 0;
                fifo_queue[i] = i; // Initialize FIFO queue

            fifo_index = 0;
            replaced_line = 0;

            if (policy_select == 2'b00) begin // LRU
                replaced_line = 0; // Find the least recently used line
                for (i = 1; i < 16; i = i + 1) begin
                    if (lru_counter[i] < lru_counter[replaced_line]) begin
                        replaced_line = i;
                    end

                lru_counter[replaced_line] = 0; // Reset this line's counter
                for (i = 0; i < 16; i = i + 1) begin
                    if (i != replaced_line) lru_counter[i] = lru_counter[i] + 1; // Update other counters
                end
            end else if (policy_select == 2'b01) begin // FIFO
                replaced_line = fifo_queue[fifo_index];
                fifo_index = (fifo_index + 1) % 16; // Circular increment
            end
        end
    end
endmodule
